caption: A wine glass half full of water is tapped on the rim with a spoon, and the water surface inside breaks into fine ripples while the glass rings.

sa.check: A wine glass about half full of water.
A spoon taps the rim of the glass.
The water surface breaks into ripples.
The ripples are fine and small, not a large slosh.
The tap lands on the rim, not on the bowl or the stem.
The tap comes first and the ripples follow.

pc.expect: The water surface is flat and still until the spoon touches the rim; ripples appear at the tap and only then.
pc.fail: Ripples are on the surface before the spoon reaches the rim; or appear while the spoon is well away from the glass; or the spoon strikes the rim and the surface stays mirror-flat; or the water ripples again after settling with the spoon nowhere near.

pc.expect: The ripples are strongest right after the tap and fade steadily to a flat surface.
pc.fail: The ripples grow stronger after the tap with no second tap; or keep the same strength for the whole clip; or the surface goes flat and breaks up again on its own; or a fully rippled surface turns flat in a single instant.

pc.expect: The ripples are a fine pattern on the water's surface; the glass stays a rigid vessel and the water stays inside it.
pc.fail: The glass bowl flexes or wobbles like rubber at the tap; or the water sloshes as one wave up the side of the bowl; or droplets fly out of the glass.

pc.expect: The glass stands where it is; the rim tap leaves it in place and only the water surface moves.
pc.fail: The glass slides or rocks on its base at the tap; or tilts and holds the tilt; or moves across the surface it stands on with nothing touching it.
pc.precondition: The glass stands on a table or other surface rather than being held.

pc.expect: One glass, one spoon, the same amount of water; nothing passes through anything.
pc.fail: The spoon passes through the rim or into the bowl wall; or the water level jumps up or down; or a second glass appears; or the glass changes shape.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The glass's tint, the water's colour and the setting around them stay the same.
pc.fail: The water changes colour; or the glass's tint or pattern changes; or objects around the glass shift by themselves.

note: The ringing is inaudible and is not judged; the ripples are its visible sign. The caption does not say whether the glass stands or is held, so P4 applies only when it stands on a surface.
